title: Changpu Yujin Decoction Alleviates Tourette Syndrome by Modulating Lipid Metabolism and Microglial Polarization: Involvement of the TREM2/NF-kappaB Signaling Axis
evidence_type: peer-reviewed primary preclinical rat and cell study; abstract-only extraction
date_caveat: Older publication newly retrieved with October 27 indexing; history timezone not verified.
population: Juvenile rats and LPS-exposed BV2 cells, not people with Tourette.
design: Rat treatment comparison over 28 days plus separate TREM2-siRNA cell perturbation.
outcome: Stereotypy, locomotion, lipid/inflammatory markers and cellular phenotypes, not human tic disability.
numeric_results: Direction of reported changes only; no verified effect sizes or confidence intervals extracted.
mechanism: Knockdown adds experimental perturbation, but serum-associated reversal alone does not establish TREM2 necessity/sufficiency or a human causal mechanism.
claim_supported: Preclinical effects support further qualified hypothesis testing.
claim_not_supported: Human efficacy, safety, clinical dose, durable disease modification or cure; background clinical-use assertions are not clinical results of this study.
risk_of_bias: Outcome denominators, blinding, attrition and multiplicity unverified
